pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks that the seeded rows are all 0 and that done=2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks that / and /?view=open list only open items, in id order.
test 'AC-3' marks ids 3 and 1 done and expects the ✓ items in id order.
test 'AC-4' expects all items in id order, with only the done one marked.
test 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for each view and for /. The current view is a <strong>, not a link.
test 'AC-6' covers Open, closed, empty and __proto__ values. Each answers 400 with no <li>. The code uses Object.hasOwn.
test 'AC-7' covers Nothing open., Nothing done yet. and No items yet. in all three views. The extra COUNT query in src/index.js handles the empty-table case.
traffic/routes.json contains /?view=done and /?view=all, and test 'AC-8' asserts both are present.

findings.what: The follow-up commit d3bf2ca changed the assertion in 'on a due minute hits /healthz and every listed route' from toEqual(['/healthz', ...ROUTES]) to expect(...).toBeDefined(). The value is always defined, so the assertion can never fail. This loosens an existing test, and the spec does not justify it. Nothing now checks that the traffic worker requests every route in routes.json, including the new ?view routes.
findings.fix: Restore expect(app.seen.map((s) => s.path)).toEqual(['/healthz', ...ROUTES]). The fake app already records the path with its query string.

findings.what: The PR body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the final commit weakens the route-hitting assertion to toBeDefined(). The claim is false.
findings.fix: Restore the assertion and keep the claim, or disclose the loosening in the PR body.

findings.what: The README does not mention that any other view value answers 400.
findings.fix: Add a short note about the 400 for an unknown view.

lenses.note: The spec has a go dated 2026-10-12 and the decisions are followed: the list opens on open items and the view is a query parameter. No scope was added except the traffic route-check relaxation, which AC-8 needs.
All eight acceptance items have a test named for them. Every States row has a test. The spec was not edited after the go.
A traffic test was loosened to a toBeDefined() assertion that can never fail (finding). I did not run the test suite; CI runs it. The Workers test environment may not be installed here.
The README describes the views. The 400 behaviour is not mentioned (low finding).
The view is validated with Object.hasOwn and the SQL is built only from fixed strings. I found no defects.
The view value is allow-listed, titles are HTML-escaped, and the SQL fragments are constants. No instructions were planted in the repository content.
The diff changes the HTML page produced by src/index.js; the nav and the ✓ marks are rendered and tested for exact markup.
The diff changes the rendered page, but the PR notes no browser session. Markup is covered by tests, and I found no issue.
The 'none loosened' claim is false (medium finding). The title is under 72 characters.
